questions.q: 4,4-Dimethylcyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-one is heated with acid. The product is:
questions.explain: After O-protonation the positive charge sits on C-3; one methyl shifts from C-4 to C-3 and loss of H⁺ from C-3 aromatises the ring, leaving the second methyl on C-4.

questions.q: What is the driving force of the dienone–phenol rearrangement?
options: Relief of ring strain in the dienone
Formation of a stronger C=O bond
Formation of an aromatic phenol ring
questions.explain: C-4 carries two groups and no H, so the dienone cannot aromatise directly; a 1,2-shift puts an H-bearing carbon next to the cation, and losing that H⁺ gives the aromatic phenol.

questions.q: 4-Methyl-4-phenylcyclohexa-2,5-dien-1-one rearranges in acid. The main product is:
questions.explain: Phenyl migrates in preference to methyl, so phenyl moves to C-3 and methyl stays on C-4.

questions.q: A 4,4-disubstituted cyclohexa-2,5-dienone carries CH₃ and COOEt on C-4. Under acid catalysis, the phenol formed has (numbering from the OH carbon as C-1):
options: CH₃ at C-3 and COOEt at C-4
COOEt at C-2 and CH₃ at C-4
COOEt at C-3 and CH₃ at C-4
Both groups at C-4, with no shift
questions.explain: COOEt migrates ahead of alkyl: left on C-4 it would destabilise the cation that forms there, so it moves to C-3 and the methyl stays on C-4.
